issue: Under Stinson and the Guidelines commentary, may a sentencing court apply the $500-per-access-device loss multiplier in U.S.S.G. § 2B1.1 to each card a defendant possessed, including credit cards, rather than counting only the cards charged in the offense?

sides.position: The $500-per-card multiplier applies to all access devices a defendant possessed; the commentary is authoritative and its plain text controls.
cases: United States v. Moore, 788 F.3d 693 (7th Cir. 2015)

sides.position: The per-card multiplier is invalid under Stinson and Kisor because it conflicts with the Guideline's loss framework; the commentary cannot be applied this way.
cases: United States v. Kirilyuk, 29 F.4th 1128 (9th Cir. 2022)

this_court: The majority holds the per-card multiplier invalid under Stinson. The dissent identifies this as creating a split with the Seventh and Eighth Circuits.
quote: The Seventh Circuit, for instance, has held that the $500per-card multiplier applies to all access devices a defendant possesses.
cite: United States v. Ruslan Kirilyuk, 29 F.4th 1128 (9th Cir. 2022)
